title: Gold-YOLO: Efficient Object Detector via Gather-and-Distribute Mechanism

problem.summary: Single-stage YOLO detectors still suffer an information fusion problem in their FPN/PANet-style necks: cross-level fusion is done recursively, so information not selected by intermediate layers is discarded and lost, hurting fusion across scales.
statements: FPN and PANet improved multi-scale fusion but previous models still suffer from an information fusion problem.
Conventional FPN-like structures cannot transmit information without loss when fusing non-adjacent levels, which hinders better information fusion.
Previous FPN-based fusion structures still have drawbacks in low speed, cross-level information exchange, and information loss.

evidence.quote: we find previous models still suffer from information fusion problem, although Feature Pyramid Network (FPN) and Path Aggregation Network (PANet) have alleviated this.
the conventional FPN-like structure fails to transmit information without loss, which hinders YOLOs from better information fusion.
Information interactions between layers can only exchange information that is selected by intermediate layers, and not selected information is discarded during transmission.
the previous FPN-based fusion structures still have drawbacks in low speed, cross-level information exchange and information loss.
This transfer mode can result in a significant loss of information during calculation.

background.summary: The work builds on FPN and PANet necks for multi-scale fusion, on the global-fusion idea demonstrated by TopFormer in segmentation, and on reparameterized YOLOv6, claiming prior necks still lose information and exchange across levels poorly.

evidence.quote: Single-stage detection models, especially YOLO series models, have been widely welcomed in the industry due to their simple structure and balance between speed and accuracy.
High-performance and low-latency object detector is receiving increasing attention for deployment on the edge devices.

solution.summary: The paper proposes a Gather-and-Distribute (GD) mechanism that globally fuses multi-level features and injects the global information back into higher levels: a shallow convolution-based Low-GD branch and a deep attention-based High-GD branch gather/align/fuse features via FAM and IFM modules, complemented by a lightweight adjacent-layer fusion (LAF) module, forming the end-to-end Gold-YOLO detector.
solution.approach: Gather multi-level features into a global representation, distribute (inject) it back into higher levels, and add lightweight adjacent-layer fusion to complete information flow in the neck.

evidence.quote: propose a novel Gather-and-Distribute mechanism (GD) for efficient information exchanging in YOLOs by globally fusing multi-level features and injecting the global information into higher levels.

GD mechanism comprises two branches: a shallow gather-and-distribute branch and a deep gatherand-distribute branch, which extract and fuse feature information via a convolution-based block and an attention-based block, respectively.
we introduce a lightweight adjacent-layer fusion module which combines features from neighboring levels on a local scale.
The gather process involves two steps. Firstly, the FAM collects and aligns features from various levels. Secondly, IFM fuses the aligned features to generate global information.

experiments.summary: Gold-YOLO is evaluated on COCO val2017 with N/S/M/L scales (with and without self-distillation and MIM pre-training), in transfer experiments with Mask R-CNN and EfficientDet detection backbones and PointRend segmentation, and in T4/V100 latency-throughput comparisons against YOLOv5/6/7/8, YOLOX and PPYOLOE.

evidence.quote: Gold-YOLO-N attains an outstanding 39.9% AP on the COCO val2017 datasets and 1030 FPS on a T4 GPU, which outperforms the previous SOTA model YOLOv6-3.0-N with similar FPS by +2.4%.
our Gold-YOLO-S with pre-training achieves 46.4% AP, which outperforms the previous SOTA YOLOv6-3.0-S with 45.0% AP at similar speed.
Gold-YOLO-N demonstrates notable advancements, achieving an improvement of 2.6%/2.4%/6.6% compared to YOLOv8-N, YOLOv6-3.0-N, and YOLOv7-Tiny (input size=416), respectively
The Low-GD predominantly targets small and medium-sized objects, whereas the High-GD primarily detect large-sized objects, and the LAF module bolsters both branches.
All our models are trained on 8 NVIDIA A100 GPUs, and the speed performance is measured on an NVIDIA Tesla T4 GPU with TensorRT.

limitations.summary: The authors admit that finer structural adjustments could further improve performance but need significant compute, and that the algorithm's heavy use of attention may be unfriendly to earlier hardware; MIM pre-training was also skipped for the smallest model.
items: Finer structural tuning could help but requires a significant amount of computational resources.
Heavy usage of attention operations may be unfriendly to some earlier hardware support.
MIM pre-training was not employed for Gold-YOLO-N due to its small backbone's limited capacity.

evidence.quote: Generally, making finer adjustments on the structure will help further improve the model’s performance, but this requires a significant amount of computational resources.
due to our algorithm’s heavy usage of attention operations, it may not be as friendly to some earlier hardware support.
MIM pretraining was not employed for Gold-YOLO-N due to the limited capacity of its small backbone.

futureDirections.direction: Further performance improvements while keeping the network built from simple, deployment-friendly, well-validated operators.
futureDirections.quote: Moreover, this decision also creates opportunities for future performance enhancements.

applications.detail: Earlier disease diagnosis and lower initial diagnosis cost
applications.quote: In the healthcare domain, the YOLO series models can improve the early diagnosis rates of certain diseases and reduce the cost of initial diagnosis, thereby saving more lives.

applications.detail: Assists autonomous vehicle driving, traffic safety and efficiency
applications.quote: In the field of intelligent transportation, the YOLO model can assist in autonomous driving of vehicles, enhancing traffic safety and efficiency.

applications.detail: Authors flag risk of drone target recognition and reconnaissance uses
applications.quote: there are also risks associated with the military application of the YOLO model, such as target recognition for drones and assisting military reconnaissance.

evidence.quote: Single-stage detection models, especially YOLO series models, have been widely welcomed in the industry due to their simple structure and balance between speed and accuracy.
High-performance and low-latency object detector is receiving increasing attention for deployment on the edge devices.

we intentionally opted for simple and thoroughly validated structures. This choice serves to prevent potential development and performance issues arising from certain operators being unsupported by deployment devices.
